name: Fill-Rite FR1210G 12V Fuel Transfer Pump
summary: The default 12V pump for drums and transfer tanks that hold gasoline as well as diesel.
verdict: Fill-Rite has been making fuel transfer pumps for decades, and the FR1210G is its long-running 12V DC drum and tank pump. Fill-Rite rates it at 13 gallons per minute and lists it for gasoline, diesel and kerosene, which is the main reason it tops this list: many 12V pumps at lower prices are diesel-only. It comes as a kit with a discharge hose, a manual nozzle and a telescoping suction pipe, and it mounts to a standard drum bung or transfer tank opening. Power comes from a 12V battery through the supplied cable; connect it with the switch off and away from the fuel opening. Like most 12V pumps it has a duty cycle, so check the manual and let it cool between long runs. Bond and ground drums as Fill-Rite instructs when pumping gasoline. For a farm, shop or anyone refueling equipment from bulk storage, it is the pump to buy.

name: GPI M-150S 12V Fuel Transfer Pump
summary: A slightly faster alternative to the Fill-Rite for truck-bed transfer tanks.
verdict: GPI, Great Plains Industries, is the other big name in 12V fuel pumps, and the M-150S is its mainstream tank pump. GPI sells it as a 15 gallons-per-minute pump and markets it for both gasoline and diesel, which puts it in the same class as the Fill-Rite FR1210G with a little more rated flow. It is a common fit on pickup-bed transfer tanks used to refuel equipment in the field, and it ships with a discharge hose and nozzle. As with any 12V pump, wire it with the supplied cable and fuse, respect its duty cycle and bond or ground the tank as GPI's manual describes when pumping gasoline. Confirm the exact variant's fuel approvals on its label, since GPI sells several versions with different nozzles and options. For a contractor or farmer refueling machines from a truck, it is a dependable, widely supported choice.

name: TERA PUMP TRFA01 Battery Powered Fuel Transfer Pump
summary: The pump most homeowners actually need for refueling a generator or mower from cans.
verdict: TERA PUMP's TRFA01 is a handheld battery operated transfer pump built for the job most homeowners face: moving fuel from a five-gallon can into a generator, mower, outboard or ATV without lifting the can. The pump tube goes into the can, a hose runs to the target tank, and the batteries in the handle drive a small impeller. TERA PUMP markets it for gasoline, diesel and kerosene; check the current listing and manual for the exact fuels and any ethanol limits before use. Flow is modest by drum-pump standards, which is actually an advantage when the target is a narrow generator fill neck. Owners commonly use it during outages to refuel generators quickly and cleanly. Use it only with the generator shut off and cool, with the can on the ground outdoors. For anyone who only handles cans, it does the job without the expense or wiring of a 12V pump.

name: GPI M-180S-EF 12V Fuel Transfer Pump
summary: For farms and fleets that refuel big diesel equipment and want the fastest fills.
verdict: The GPI M-180S-EF is the high-flow member of GPI's 12V M-series, sold as an 18 gallons-per-minute pump for transfer tanks and drums. It is aimed at farms, construction sites and fleets where big diesel equipment has large tanks and waiting on a slower pump costs real time. Because it draws more current than the smaller pumps, wiring and battery condition matter more: use the supplied cable and fuse, run it from a healthy battery, and observe the duty cycle in GPI's manual. GPI markets the M-series for gasoline and diesel, but compatibility can differ between variants and options, so confirm the exact model's approved fuels and ethanol limits on its label before pumping gasoline. Bond and ground tanks as instructed. For a homeowner with a generator, this is far more pump than needed; for anyone filling a tractor or skid steer every day, it is the one to consider.

name: Fill-Rite FR112 Rotary Hand Pump
summary: The no-power drum pump every farm or shop with bulk fuel should keep as a backup.
verdict: The Fill-Rite FR112 is a manual rotary hand pump that threads into a standard drum bung and moves fuel with each turn of its crank. It has no motor and no wiring, so it works whether or not a 12V battery is handy and keeps electrical parts out of the vapor zone entirely. That makes it a durable primary pump for a drum of diesel or kerosene in a barn or shop, and a sensible backup to a 12V pump for when the battery is flat. It is slower and more tiring than any electric pump, which matters when filling large tanks, and it has no auto-stop, so watch the receiving tank closely. Fill-Rite sells several variants; confirm on the label that the one you buy is approved for the fuel you plan to pump, especially gasoline, and bond and ground the drum as the manual describes.
